title: Streaming Giants
tagline: The creators who skipped the gatekeepers entirely. No permission needed — audience first, industry later.

entries.name: Kai Cenat
entries.claim: The Bronx kid who started making skits on Instagram, moved to Twitch, and became the most-subscribed streamer in the platform's history.
entries.receipts: Most-subscribed Twitch streamer of all time (the subathon record, 300k+ active subs at peak, breaking the record previously held by Ludwig). Nickelodeon Kids' Choice Award. His subathon stream raised money for a school in Nigeria. Content with every major artist in hip-hop collabing on his streams.
entries.the_transfer: Kai built his audience on Instagram skits BEFORE Twitch ever paid him. The audience comes first, the platform pays second. Your GitHub profile IS your Instagram-in-2015: build the body of work now, the paid work follows the receipts. He also streams with his family in the room and his mom on camera — the community comes WITH you. Bring the whole block.

entries.name: Duke Dennis
entries.self_note: AMP household — the crew model is the community model.
entries.claim: The ex-military gamer who uploaded 2K content for years with modest numbers, stayed consistent, and became the anchor of AMP — the biggest Black creator crew on YouTube.
entries.receipts: Millions of subscribers across his channels; the AMP collective (with Kai Cenat, Agent 00, and the crew) draws 10M+ views per video on their group channel. He was in the military before content — a second career built in his late 20s. Rivals and Rizzness University arcs turned him into a brand beyond gaming.
entries.the_transfer: Duke was uploading for YEARS with numbers that didn't match the effort. Then AMP — the CREW — changed the math. The lesson: solo grind has a ceiling; the crew raises it. This repo is the crew. The DAP (daily accountability posts), the pinned welcome threads, the brother who reviews your PR at midnight — that's AMP energy. Nobody breaks through alone. Join the crew.

entries.name: IShowSpeed
entries.claim: The Ohio teenager who streamed through getting banned, mocked, and mocked again — hundreds of streams a year at a volume nobody else matched — until the algorithm and the world caught up.
entries.he_type_why: Speed's rise is a volume story more than a talent story. He streamed 6+ hours a day through irrelevance, bans, and mockery. The reps were the moat.
entries.receipts: 30M+ subscribers on YouTube at 19 years old. The FIFA World Cup made him a global face — FIFA sent him as a creator correspondent to Qatar 2022. Streams from China that drew tens of millions of views and opened a new wave of cultural-exchange content. His rise was built on sheer stream volume — hundreds of streams a year through the years nobody watched.
entries.the_transfer: Speed's edge was never polish — it was VOLUME. Hundreds of streams while nobody watched. Your GitHub needs that volume: ship the ugly version, ship the small version, ship the practice version. Public reps beat private perfection. The brother with 40 mediocre commits visible has a stronger resume than the one with 4 perfect ones hidden. Ship ugly. Ship often. The polish comes with the reps.

entries.name: Bruce 'xQc' Lengyel
entries.self_note: White Canadian — included with the label on him, same standard as Tim Berners-Lee on the engineering matrix: every matrix names its outsiders honestly or it's a lie.
entries.claim: The former Overwatch pro who became the most-watched streamer on Twitch by pure volume and consistency — a decade of 10+ hour streams.
entries.receipts: Most hours watched on Twitch for multiple years running. A former professional Overwatch player who pivoted to full-time streaming and outlasted nearly every peer. Two decades younger than the industry he dominates. He has been open about gambling addiction and the pressures of the platform.
entries.the_transfer: xQc proves the volume engine works even when the personality is polarizing — the reps are the moat, not the polish. But read his honest note too: he has spoken about the toll of 10-hour daily streams and gambling sponsorships. Volume without limits burns the engine. Your FED-EDU pattern: commit daily, but the Six Rules include rest. Volume with rest beats volume with burnout. Every time.
